claims.claim: Quintus Septimius Florens Tertullianus, known as Tertullian, was a Carthaginian Christian writer born around 155‑160 AD and died after 220 AD.
The work was written to warn and instruct Christian believers about the inevitability of heresies and to show how to counter them using apostolic Scripture.
In the treatise Tertullian argues that heretics have no right to use Scripture because it belongs only to the legitimate apostolic churches.
The work survives in Latin manuscripts and has been preserved in modern collections such as the Ante‑Nicene Fathers (Vol. III) and in English translations on sites like New Advent and Tertullian.org.

The Prescription against Heretics is significant because it introduces a legal metaphor of “prescription” to block heretical arguments and it helped shape early Western Christian polemics against heresy.
